subject: Business Models
title: Decentralized Marketplaces
description: A quick win: understand Decentralized Marketplaces.

hook.text: What if eBay had no owner? Blockchain-based marketplaces run on code, not corporate boards.

buildup.text: Decentralized marketplaces use smart contracts: automated rules that execute transactions without a middleman.

discovery.text: OpenSea for NFTs showed this works—$23 billion in trading volume with minimal human intervention.

twist.text: OpenSea's volume crashed 99% from its peak. Decentralized doesn't mean demand-proof.

climax.text: Decentralized marketplaces reduce fees but struggle with trust, curation, and dispute resolution.

punchline.text: No middleman, no fees—but also no one to call when things go wrong.

quiz.question: What is the main trade-off with decentralized marketplaces?
options: Lower fees but weaker trust and dispute resolution

details.summary: Decentralized marketplaces use blockchain technology to enable peer-to-peer transactions without a central platform operator. Smart contracts handle escrow, dispute resolution, and payments automatically..
details.whyItMatters: Decentralized marketplaces challenge the assumption that marketplace platforms need to be controlled by a single company..
takeaways: Blockchain enables peer-to-peer marketplace transactions without central operators
Smart contracts automate escrow, payments, and basic dispute resolution
Poor user experience and low liquidity limit decentralized marketplace adoption

faq.question: What advantages do decentralized marketplaces claim over centralized ones?
faq.answer: Lower fees since there is no platform extracting commissions. Censorship resistance since no central authority can remove listings. User data ownership since no company collects transaction histories. Transparent rules encoded in smart contracts rather than changeable corporate policies.

faq.question: Why haven't decentralized marketplaces achieved mainstream adoption?
faq.answer: Poor user experience requiring crypto wallets and blockchain knowledge. Low liquidity since most buyers and sellers are on centralized platforms. No recourse for scams beyond what smart contracts can detect. Slower transaction speeds than centralized systems. Lack of customer support.
